FAQ

Questions, answered.

Is Onyx free?

Yes. Onyx itself is completely free. The AI services you connect keep their own plans and limits — Onyx shows your usage so you always know where you stand.

Do I need an Onyx account?

No. There's no Onyx account and no sign-up. Each AI uses its own official sign-in (for example, your ChatGPT or Claude account) through its command-line tool.

Which AIs does Onyx support?

Claude Code, ChatGPT (via the Codex CLI) and OpenCode out of the box — including all their models and thinking levels. You can also add any other AI command-line tool as a custom provider.

Where is my data stored?

Your chats and settings stay on your computer. Onyx doesn't have servers and doesn't collect analytics. Your messages go only to the AI provider you choose.

Can the AI change files on my computer?

Only if you let it. Choose Local for full access, Folder or File to limit it to one place, or turn on Read-only so it can only look and suggest.

Why does Windows or macOS show a warning when I install?

Onyx is new and its installers aren't code-signed yet, so your system asks you to confirm. On Windows click More info → Run anyway; on macOS right-click the app and choose Open.

How do I update Onyx?

Download the latest version from this page and install it over the old one. Your chats and settings are kept.
